name: Amazon Bedrock

auth.notes: Classic auth is AWS Signature Version 4 over the whole request (service name 'bedrock'), computed from access key id + secret access key (+ session token for temporary creds); the broker must sign each request, not just add a header. Bedrock API keys (2025+) are simpler: Authorization: Bearer <key>, read from AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK.

key_format.example_shape: Access key id AKIA<16 uppercase letters/digits> + 40-character secret; or a Bedrock API key
key_format.notes: The regex is for the access key id only. AKIA = long-term IAM user key, ASIA = temporary (needs session token). ABSK as the long-term Bedrock API key prefix is from secret-scanner knowledge, not confirmed in the docs I read.

verify.notes: ListFoundationModels control-plane call; read-only. Needs bedrock:ListFoundationModels permission, which a narrowly scoped IAM key may lack (403 then means 'valid but not permitted'). An alternative signature-only check is STS GetCallerIdentity at sts.amazonaws.com.

safe_default: Allow POST /model/*/converse, /model/*/converse-stream, /model/*/invoke, /model/*/invoke-with-response-stream on bedrock-runtime.<region>; GET /foundation-models; block the rest
notes: An IAM access key may grant far more than Bedrock; strongly prefer a Bedrock API key or an IAM user limited to bedrock:Invoke*. Bedrock API keys cannot be used with InvokeModelWithBidirectionalStream, Agents or Data Automation APIs.

name: Coinbase Developer Platform (CDP)

auth.notes: Secret API key (key id + secret) signs a per-request JWT (Ed25519, valid 2 min, bound to method+host+path), sent as Authorization: Bearer <JWT>.
